channel.title: Desk Draw Updates
channel.description: Signed Desk Draw releases for macOS.

item.description:
🤖 Claude Opus 5.5 responding on behalf of Nils 🤘🏻
No more Screen Recording prompts after updates.
- Until now, macOS asked to allow Screen Recording again after every update, even though Desk Draw was still listed as allowed. Desk Draw is now signed with its own certificate, so macOS recognizes updated versions as the same app and keeps the permission. - After updating to 0.6.1, macOS asks one last time. Allow Desk Draw under System Settings → Privacy & Security → Screen Recording, then quit and reopen it. Later updates keep the permission.
Requires macOS 14 or later on Apple Silicon. This build is signed with Desk Draw's own certificate and not notarized; macOS may require **Open Anyway** on first launch.

🤖 Claude Opus 5.5 responding on behalf of Nils 🤘🏻
Number the steps you point out.
- The new **Number** tool (**N**) places a colored dot with a number in it at each click: 1, 2, 3 and so on. Drag before letting go to place it exactly. - The next number is always one more than the highest number there, so removing a dot never leads to two with the same number. Once all dots are gone, counting starts at 1 again. - Dots use the current color and size, and stay readable on any background and on the whiteboard. - Like any mark, a dot can be selected, moved, resized and restyled, with undo. - The screenshot's JSON file lists each dot's number, so an AI agent can match "step 3" to its place.
Requires macOS 14 or later on Apple Silicon. This build is ad-hoc signed and not notarized; macOS may require **Open Anyway** on first launch and renewed Screen Recording permission after an update.

🤖 Claude Opus 5.5 responding on behalf of Nils 🤘🏻
Fixes closing an unsaved whiteboard.
- The question whether to save or discard an unsaved whiteboard now appears in front of the board. Before, it could open hidden behind the board, so Esc, the close button and the hotkey seemed to do nothing and Desk Draw stopped responding. - The question now appears on the display you are drawing on.
Requires macOS 14 or later on Apple Silicon. This build is ad-hoc signed and not notarized; macOS may require **Open Anyway** on first launch and renewed Screen Recording permission after an update.

🤖 Claude Opus 5.5 responding on behalf of Nils 🤘🏻
Desk Draw now has a whiteboard.
- Click the new whiteboard button in the toolbar, or press **B**, to cover the display with a white board. All tools work on it, and white ink switches to black so it stays visible. - Press **⌘S** or click **Save** to save the whole board as an image. It goes to the screenshots folder, is copied to the clipboard, and needs no Screen Recording permission. - Press **B** again to go back to drawing on the screen. Your marks stay. - A whiteboard with unsaved drawings is never discarded by accident. **Esc**, the close button, **⌥⇧D**, **Stop Drawing** and **Quit** first ask whether to save it, discard it or keep drawing. - If the display layout changes while you draw, an unsaved whiteboard is saved before drawing stops.
Requires macOS 14 or later on Apple Silicon. This build is ad-hoc signed and not notarized; macOS may require **Open Anyway** on first launch and renewed Screen Recording permission after an update.

🤖 Claude Opus 5.5 responding on behalf of Nils 🤘🏻
Everything you draw can now be changed after you draw it.
- Pick the new **Select** tool (**V**) and click a mark to select it. - Drag a mark to move it, or nudge it with the arrow keys (Shift moves 10 points). - Drag a handle to resize it. Shift keeps the proportions, or snaps lines and arrows to 45° steps. Dragging a corner of text scales its font. - Pick a color, size or fill to restyle the selected mark. Selecting a mark shows its current style in the toolbar. - Press **⌫** to delete the selected mark, or **Esc** to deselect it. - Picking a color or size while typing text now applies it to that text.
Every change can be undone.
Requires macOS 14 or later on Apple Silicon. This build is ad-hoc signed and not notarized; macOS may require **Open Anyway** on first launch and renewed Screen Recording permission after an update.

🤖 Written and posted by GPT-6.1 Sol (OpenAI, effort: high) on behalf of Nils.
Desk Draw can now check for updates and install them with Sparkle.
- Use **Check for Updates…** in the menu bar menu, or leave automatic checks enabled. - Choose whether to download and install updates automatically. Your choice is remembered. - Updates wait for an active drawing session to finish before restarting the app. - Update archives and the update feed are cryptographically signed and verified before use.
Versions 0.1.0 and 0.2.0 need one manual update to this version. Subsequent updates can be installed from the app.
Requires macOS 14 or later on Apple Silicon. This build is ad-hoc signed and not notarized; macOS may require **Open Anyway** on first launch and renewed Screen Recording permission after an update.
